To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C-5 glutamyl-tRNareductase (GluTR) gene from Rhodospirlum rubrum was successfully expressed in Rhodobactere sphaeroidess O.U.001 and the recombinant strain produced more 5-aminolaevulinic acid (ALA) and hydrogen.
we have developed a new bacterial strain producing more amounts of 5-ALa and biohydrogen by heterologous expression of the gene encoding glutamyl-t RNA reductase in R. s phaeroides.
we have successfully engineered the R. sphaeoides genome to enable it to synthesize 5-ALA using the C-5 route.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new and unique R. sphaeoides strain for the production of both 5-ALA and H2, which can be used in the pharmaceutical and fuel industries.
the development of a bioprocess that produces two valuable products (H2 and 5-ALA) from a single substrate, using a single bacterial strain.
the production of 5-ala and biohydrogen using R. sphaeorides O.U.001 as a model strain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of the glutamyl-t-RNA reductase gene of R. rubrum in R. spheroides O.U001, a bacterium that synthesizes 5ALA via the C-4 route, resulted in an increase of the 5ALA production and the expression of the C-4 and C-5 pathways.
the modified strain produced more 5-ALAs and less H2, while the wild-type strain did the opposite.
the expression of the glutamyl-t-RNA reductase gene enabled the C-5 5-ALA pathway in R. spheroides and resulted in an increase of 5- ALA production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-5 5-ALA production pathway is functional in the modified R. sphae-roides O.U. 001 strain and that the bioprocess for 5-ALA and biohydrogen production was optimized.
the C-5 and C-4 pathways were both active in the modified strain, whereas the C-4 alone was active in the wild-type strain.
a new bacterial strain was developed to produce 5-ALA and biohydrogen in the same process using a biorefining approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-5 5-ALA pathway was successfully engineered in the photosynthetic bacterium R. sphae-roides to enhance 5-A LA production.
the C-5 glutamyl-tRNareductase pathway is functional in R. spheroides and can be exploited to enhance 5ALA production.
a new strain of R. sphaeroide was engineered to enhance 5-amino levulinic acid production by enabling a new pathway, the C-4 and C-5 pathways.
